text:
alex_w: quick heads-up — saw a recurring tail-latency bump on Mistral-7B when using sliding-window attention + rope scaling. spike happens around the window boundary (seq ~ 2048 -> 2560). about 17% p99 increase vs baseline. reproducer: hosted ded pool with kv-cache enabled, batch size 12, steady stream rps.
maya.k: oof. any kernel switch logs? sounds like kernel selector flipping mid-request could invalidate kv cache pointers.
samir_p: can you paste the profiler snapshot? even a flame or the kernel decision trace helps.
alex_w: dropping the sampling output. note that this is NOT model weight change, just inference config.

alex_w: ```
# perf snippet
request_seq=2500
batch=12
kernel_selector: pre-emit -> matmul_opt_v2 @ token 2499
kernel_selector: fallback -> matmul_generic @ token 2501
kv_cache.evicted_entries: 0
kv_cache.ptr_shift: true
latencies_ms: [1.2,1.1,1.3,...,4.6,5.2]  # tail spikes after token 2500
``` 

jin: hm `kv_cache.ptr_shift: true` stands out — sounds like our sliding-window offset normalization moved base index and some kernels expect non-wrapped indices.
maya.k: agreed. this feels like a rope-scaling interaction: when RoPE scaling reduces effective positions, our `max_position_embeddings` guard kicks in and we end up with position remap that breaks tiled-kv pointer math.
samir_p: can you repro with `--no-rope-rescale` or force `max_pos=4096`? if the change disappears then it's definitely position transform related.
alex_w: quick test: forced `no_rescale` removes spike (p99 back to baseline). forcing `max_pos=4096` reduces but doesn't fully eliminate — still a small jitter.

maya.k: hypothesis: the kernel cost model chooses different matmul kernel depending on sequence window size. after rope-rescale it computes an apparent shorter seq (or it triggers different tiling) and our batched cache offset math doesn't apply the same pointer normalization -> later requests reuse stale KV tiles and need extra remap, causing micro-copy/fallback.

jin: proposed mitigations:
- add a small cooldown window after any kernel switch where we keep original kernel for N tokens per-req
- make KV pointer math tolerant to index wrap/offset (normalize per-tile)
- add a cheap pre-check: if `rope_rescale` changed `pos_index_map` between steps, prefer generic kernel that handles pointer shifts

samir_p: also add a metric: `kernel_switch_rate_per_req` and correlate with `kv_ptr_normalizations` and `tail_latency_delta`. quick dashboard will justify the change.
alex_w: I'll run an A/B with `cooldown=8` tokens and the pre-check. expected result: drop p99 by ~12% on our trafficked prompt set.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: feature/kv-robustness -> staging (sha: a1b2c3d)

maya.k: one extra gotcha — some of our heuristics assume steady sequence-length distribution; but chat completions with trimmed context can cause oscillations across window boundaries. Suggest we add sequence-length jitter tests in perf suite.

alex_w: agreed. i'll add a microbenchmark: repeated sliding-window wrap at boundary with varying rope scales and 3 kernel candidates. will post results here.

samir_p: neat. if you can capture `kernel_selector` decisions + `kv_ptr` snapshots per token for 2000-2600 seq window, we can probably craft a minimal repro and a unit test.

jin: thanks — if we validate this is pointer-normalization bug, we can fix pointer math first then only use cooldown as temporary mitigation.

alex_w: timeline: run tests today, open PR tomorrow with pointer normalization patch + dashboard tile. tagging @maya.k and @samir_p to review.
maya.k: :thumbsup:
samir_p: ack
